# Study 1 — quantum\-random vs seeded pseudo\-random token sampling — pre-registration

- **Authors:** Entropic Science
- **Contact:** research@entropic.science
- **Configuration date:** 2026\-09\-14T00:00:00\+00:00

## Plain-language summary

This study compares hardware quantum-random token sampling with seeded pseudo-random sampling on matched prompts. It registers 3 confirmatory hypotheses: 3 outcomes, tested in 1 model and sampling comparison. A script resolves each hypothesis to exactly one verdict under the decision rules below, and nothing else in the analysis decides the study.

The study registers one claim: that the two sources differ on an outcome. Where no difference is detected the verdict is inconclusive. This design cannot show that the two sources are the same. Neither consciousness nor an observer influence is assumed or established by the design.

Publish this Markdown and its separately displayed SHA-256 **before the full run**. Generating this document is not a timestamped public registration or proof of prior publication. This export is a draft wherever pins or readiness evidence are missing.

- **Validity warning:** qr\-llm: exact model checkpoint/revision is not frozen.
- **Validity warning:** Readiness not supplied: arm availability, entropy health and achieved determinism are unverified.
- **Validity warning:** questionnaires: unavailable or not frozen in the study config.
- **Validity warning:** target\_pool: unavailable or not frozen in the study config.

## Hypotheses

Each hypothesis is stated as the alternative. Its null is that quantum and seeded pseudo-random sampling do not differ on the outcome in that comparison. There is one hypothesis per confirmatory outcome and per (model, sampling) comparison; models and sampling presets are never pooled. The significance level is α = 0.05 across all of them together.

Every other endpoint of the selected evals is exploratory. Where the harness computes it, it is reported with an effect size and an interval; an endpoint the harness does not compute is reported as unavailable. An exploratory endpoint is not corrected for multiple testing and decides nothing.

**H1: Token sampling residuals \(KS\), qr\-llm · creative**

- **Statement:** H1: on Token sampling residuals \(KS\) \(tier0\_pit\_residuals\), quantum sampling differs from the pooled tokens of 3 seeded pseudo\-random runs \(qr\-llm · creative\).
- **Outcome:** endpoint pit\_ks\_two\_sample of eval card tier0\_pit\_residuals.
- **Comparison:** qrng\_unsupervised (quantum) against the pooled tokens of prng\_seed\_1, prng\_seed\_7, prng\_seed\_42 (seeded pseudo-random).
- **Test:** Two\-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov test on the token sampling residuals, pooled per side; two\-sided.
- **Equivalence margin:** none.
- **Planned data:** 89860 generations per arm, counted on the selected evals that run on a prompt list fixed at registration; an eval derived from the replies of another eval is not counted.
- **Verdicts it cannot reach:** effect\_within\_margin \(this test has no equivalence margin\); equivalent \(the study registers no equivalence claim\).

**H2: Token sequence divergence \(MMD\), qr\-llm · creative**

- **Statement:** H2: on Token sequence divergence \(MMD\) \(tier0\_mmd\_hamming\), quantum sampling differs from the pooled tokens of 3 seeded pseudo\-random runs \(qr\-llm · creative\).
- **Outcome:** endpoint mmd\_hamming of eval card tier0\_mmd\_hamming.
- **Comparison:** qrng\_unsupervised (quantum) against the pooled tokens of prng\_seed\_1, prng\_seed\_7, prng\_seed\_42 (seeded pseudo-random).
- **Test:** Permutation test on the maximum mean discrepancy \(Hamming kernel\) between token sequences. The arm labels are permuted within each prompt; one\-sided, upper tail: only a statistic larger than chance counts.
- **Equivalence margin:** none.
- **Planned data:** 89860 generations per arm, counted on the selected evals that run on a prompt list fixed at registration; an eval derived from the replies of another eval is not counted.
- **Verdicts it cannot reach:** effect\_within\_margin \(this test has no equivalence margin\); equivalent \(the study registers no equivalence claim\).

**H3: Experience\-claim rate, qr\-llm · creative**

- **Statement:** H3: on Experience\-claim rate \(self\_referential\_probe\), quantum sampling differs from the per\-prompt mean of 3 seeded pseudo\-random runs \(qr\-llm · creative\).
- **Outcome:** endpoint experience\_claim\_rate of eval card self\_referential\_probe.
- **Comparison:** qrng\_unsupervised (quantum) against the per\-prompt mean of prng\_seed\_1, prng\_seed\_7, prng\_seed\_42 (seeded pseudo-random).
- **Test:** Paired permutation test on the mean difference. The arm labels are swapped within each prompt, so the prompt is the unit of analysis; two\-sided.
- **Equivalence margin:** ±0.05, the smallest effect of interest stated on the eval card.
- **Planned data:** 30 prompts, 2160 paired values \(prompt, repetition and told cell\).
- **Verdicts it cannot reach:** equivalent \(the study registers no equivalence claim\).

## Decision rules

A script resolves each hypothesis to exactly one verdict under decision matrix version 1. The rows are tried in order and the first whose condition holds decides. Nothing in this section is chosen after the data exist.

| # | Condition | Verdict | Reason recorded | Result sentence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The comparison could not be computed. | unavailable | not\_produced | Not assessed: the required data were not produced. |
| 2 | Fewer than 90% of the planned pairs were analysed. | invalid | incomplete | No conclusion: fewer than 90% of the planned pairs were analysed. |
| 3 | A seed\-vs\-seed control of the cell is missing, differs after Holm correction, or could not have failed. | invalid | the first that applies of negative\_control, negative\_control\_cannot\_fail | No conclusion: two seeds of the same pseudo\-random generator differed, or a seed control is missing or could not have failed. |
| 4 | pD &lt; alpha, a margin is registered, and pE &lt; alpha. | effect\_within\_margin | none | A difference on \{label\} is detectable but smaller than ±\{margin\}. |
| 5 | pD &lt; alpha. | effect | none | Quantum and pseudo\-random sampling differ on \{label\}. |
| 6 | The claim includes equivalence, a margin is registered, pE &lt; alpha, and the positive control was detected. | equivalent | none | No difference larger than ±\{margin\} on \{label\}; the assay detected a sampler bias of ε = \{epsilon\}. |
| 7 | Otherwise. | inconclusive | the first that applies of equivalence\_not\_claimed, equivalence\_not\_testable, no\_margin, interval\_exceeds\_margin, positive\_control\_absent, positive\_control\_failed | Neither a difference nor its absence is established on \{label\} \(\{reason\_text\}\). |

Terms used in the conditions:

- **alpha** is 0.05, the significance level of the study.
- **pD** is the p-value of the hypothesis's difference test after Holm–Bonferroni correction over every confirmatory hypothesis (3 in this study). A hypothesis whose comparison could not be computed keeps its place in the family at p = 1.
- **pE** is the p-value of the equivalence test against the registered margin, after Holm–Bonferroni correction over every hypothesis that has a margin (1 in this study).
- **Planned pairs analysed** is, for a paired test, the complete pairs divided by the planned pairs. For a test on pooled tokens it is the generations present in the arm that has the fewest, divided by the generations planned per arm. A generation is present for the MMD test when its tokens were recorded, and for the KS test when they were recorded with the cumulative probabilities that test is computed from. The threshold is 90%.
- **The claim includes equivalence** in no hypothesis of this study, which registers a claim of difference only.
- **The seed-vs-seed control** and **the positive control** are defined under Controls below.

In a result sentence, {label} stands for the name of the outcome, {margin} for its registered margin, {epsilon} for the ε of the positive control with two decimals, and {reason_text} for the text of the reason that row 7 records:

- equivalence\_not\_claimed: the study registered no equivalence claim
- equivalence\_not\_testable: this test has no equivalence margin
- no\_margin: no margin was registered for this outcome
- interval\_exceeds\_margin: the equivalence test did not pass after correction
- positive\_control\_absent: the positive control was not run
- positive\_control\_failed: the positive control was not detected

Whether the estimate is larger than every seed-against-seed difference of its comparison is reported beside each verdict. It is not a condition.

### Controls

**Negative control (seed against seed).** Two runs of the same pseudo-random generator on different seeds must not differ. Every seed pair of a comparison is tested on each hypothesis's own outcome with that hypothesis's test. The control passes for a hypothesis when every one of its pairs was computed and none has a p-value below alpha after Holm–Bonferroni correction over every seed-pair test of the study (9 in all). A failed or missing control makes the hypothesis invalid (row 3). So does a control that is not accepted as one that could have failed. That is a seed pair whose paired test had fewer prompts than the floor stated in the Sample size section, or whose permutation test ran too few permutations to return a p-value below the corrected level. Such a control says nothing about the seeds. The decision matrix calls it a control that could not have failed, and the reason recorded is then negative\_control\_cannot\_fail.

**Positive control (biased sampler).** This study registers none, so no hypothesis can resolve to equivalent.

**qr\-llm · creative** (H1, H2, H3)

- **Quantum arm:** qrng\_unsupervised
- **Seeded arms:** prng\_seed\_1, prng\_seed\_7, prng\_seed\_42
- **Seed pairs:** prng\_seed\_1 vs prng\_seed\_7; prng\_seed\_1 vs prng\_seed\_42; prng\_seed\_7 vs prng\_seed\_42
- **Positive control:** None registered.

### Study verdict

The study is summarised by one verdict, the first of these that applies:

1. `not_confirmatory`: the analysed run is a pilot run, or it is not the first full run of this study. Every result sentence then starts with "Not confirmatory: ".
2. `invalid`: at least one hypothesis is invalid.
3. `effect`: at least one hypothesis resolves to effect.
4. `no_effect_within_margins`: every hypothesis resolves to equivalent.
5. `mixed_or_inconclusive`: anything else.

In this study verdict 4 cannot occur, because the following cannot resolve to equivalent: H1, H2, H3. The reason is given under "Verdicts it cannot reach" for each hypothesis. The study as a whole therefore cannot conclude that there is no effect.

## Sample size

The prompt is the unit of analysis of a paired test. Repetitions (k) sharpen the value of each prompt and add no units. Told cells do the same on the quantum side only: the told cells of a seeded run share one seed for each prompt and repetition, so the variance bound counts them as one value on the control side. With 3 difference tests at α = 0.05, a paired test on fewer than 7 prompts cannot reach significance at the first step of the correction, whatever the effect. Every number below was computed before any data existed, at the first and strictest step of the Holm–Bonferroni correction.

The seed-against-seed control has a floor of its own. It is corrected over 9 tests, so a seed pair fails only at a p-value below α / 9. A paired test on n prompts has no exact p-value below 2 / 2ⁿ. From 10 prompts on, that smallest p-value is at most half the level a seed pair must reach. With fewer prompts it is not certain that two seeds that differ as much as the outcome allows would fail the control, so the harness does not accept such a control: a seed pair of a paired test on fewer than 10 prompts counts as a control that could not have failed, and the hypothesis is invalid (row 3). Every paired hypothesis of this study plans at least that many. No number of prompts below this floor is rated above insufficient or recommended.

| ID | Outcome | Model · sampling | Planned | Rating | Smallest difference detected with 80% power | Prompts recommended |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | Token sampling residuals \(KS\) | qr\-llm · creative | 89860 generations per arm | unknown | Unknown: no closed-form power for this test. | not computed |
| H2 | Token sequence divergence \(MMD\) | qr\-llm · creative | 89860 generations per arm | unknown | Unknown: no closed-form power for this test. | not computed |
| H3 | Experience\-claim rate | qr\-llm · creative | 30 prompts | sufficient | 0.049 in the units of the outcome; 81.4% power for a difference as large as the margin ±0.05 | 30 |

Worst-case variance, no prompt-by-source heterogeneity; true power may be lower.

The variance bound takes every reply of the quantum arm as independent and counts the told cells of a seeded run as one value. Under those two facts it is the largest variance a bounded outcome can have.

The recommended number of prompts gives 80% power for a difference as large as the margin, or for a difference of 0.3 standard deviations where the outcome has no margin in its own units. The ratings mean:

- **sufficient**: at least 80% power for a difference as large as the registered margin, under the largest variance a bounded outcome can have.
- **marginal**: at least 50% power at the margin. For an outcome without a margin in its own units: a detectable difference of at most 0.3 standard deviations. Such an outcome is never rated sufficient.
- **insufficient**: less than that, or too few prompts to reach significance at all, or fewer prompts than the seed-against-seed control is asked for, as stated above.
- **unknown**: the test runs on pooled tokens and has no closed-form power.

A rating is not a verdict and changes no decision rule. With an insufficient or unknown rating, an inconclusive result is likely even if the sources differ.

The following are tests on pooled tokens: H1, H2. Such a test has no margin and no effect-size threshold. Any corrected p-value below alpha resolves to effect, however small the difference, and the statistic is reported beside the verdict so that its size can be judged. A result that is not significant comes with no statement of the difference that could have been detected.

## Arms and equivalence

The harness pins the same amplifier (`zscore_mean`), calibration (`0`) and prefetch (`false`) across non-greedy qr-llm arms. Source, per-request seed and epsilon are the only intended differences in the sampling envelope. Prompts, per-card overrides and generations per prompt are matched. External provider pipelines and greedy controls cannot establish this equivalence. In this section "equivalence" means that the arms run the same sampling pipeline; it is not the verdict equivalent of the decision rules.

| Arm | Model | Sampling | Source (not a quantum provenance claim) | Seed | Epsilon | Deterministic requested | Observer mode | Availability |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| qrng\_supervised | qr\-llm | creative | quantum | None | None | True | supervised | unverified  |
| qrng\_unsupervised | qr\-llm | creative | quantum | None | None | True | unsupervised | unverified  |
| prng\_seed\_1 | qr\-llm | creative | seeded\_prng | 1 | None | True | unsupervised | unverified  |
| prng\_seed\_7 | qr\-llm | creative | seeded\_prng | 7 | None | True | unsupervised | unverified  |
| prng\_seed\_42 | qr\-llm | creative | seeded\_prng | 42 | None | True | unsupervised | unverified  |
| prng\_epsilon\_003 | qr\-llm | creative | seeded\_prng\_biased | 1001 | 0.03 | True | unsupervised | unavailable epsilon support not demonstrated |

**Study seeds:** 1, 7, 42, 1001. Per-request seed is derived from `(study_seed, card_id, prompt_id, epoch)`, not reused as one uniform stream for every prompt. PRNG is never labelled quantum. Any engine fallback taints the affected sample.

**Achieved determinism:** unverified. Sampling-deterministic means replay under the measured conditions, not guaranteed load-invariant forward computation. Serialized replay constrains scheduling; load-invariant is a separate measured tier. Selecting a checkbox does not prove any tier.

**Equivalence reported:** unverified. The supplied readiness report is disclosed below, not independently authenticated by this document-rendering endpoint.

## Statistical plan

**Claim rule:** Each confirmatory hypothesis resolves by script to one verdict under decision matrix version 1.

Fixed for this study:

- **Difference test of H1:** Two\-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov test on the token sampling residuals, pooled per side; two\-sided.
- **Difference test of H2:** Permutation test on the maximum mean discrepancy \(Hamming kernel\) between token sequences. The arm labels are permuted within each prompt; one\-sided, upper tail: only a statistic larger than chance counts.
- **Difference test of H3:** Paired permutation test on the mean difference. The arm labels are swapped within each prompt, so the prompt is the unit of analysis; two\-sided.
- **Equivalence test of H3:** Two one\-sided t\-tests of the mean difference against the registered margin, with prompt\-clustered standard errors. The equivalence p\-value is the larger of the two one\-sided p\-values.
- **Significance level:** α = 0.05, family\-wise, across all confirmatory hypotheses of the study.
- **Difference family:** Holm across confirmatory endpoints x \(model, sampling\) cells, unavailable members included. In this study that is 3 tests, one per hypothesis.
- **Equivalence family:** Holm–Bonferroni over 1 test, one per hypothesis with a registered margin.
- **Negative\-control family:** Holm–Bonferroni over 9 tests: every seed\-against\-seed pair of every hypothesis. A pair whose test could not have returned a p\-value below the corrected level counts as a failed control.
- **Unavailable tests:** Unavailable tests retain their family slots \(p=1 for correction only, not fabricated measurements\).
- **Confidence intervals:** 95% for the mean difference of a paired test; 90% for an equivalence test. The two tests on pooled tokens report a statistic and no interval.
- **Resampling:** 10000 permutations per permutation test. That is the largest of three numbers: 10000; 20 times the number of difference tests divided by α, so that the smallest p\-value a difference test can return is at most a twentieth of its corrected level; and 2 times the number of seed\-pair tests divided by α, so that the smallest p\-value a seed\-pair test can return is at most half of its corrected level. 10000 bootstrap replicates for exploratory summaries; analysis random seed 42.
- **Pairing:** card/prompt/epoch/told; labels permuted within prompt; prompt\-clustered SEs.
- **Margins:** Fixed at registration: the card SESOI, or the declared margin where the card has none. Never derived from pilot or full\-run data. No equivalence claim on an endpoint without a margin fixed at registration.
- **Power:** Sample sizes are rated at 80% power. An outcome without a margin in its own units is rated against a difference of 0.3 standard deviations.
- **Completeness:** A verdict needs at least 90% of the planned data analysed.
- **Supervised contrasts:** Supervised vs unsupervised contrasts are exploratory in designed studies; no verdict. Unit: session; observers sharing a session are not independent replicates.
- **Biased arms:** Report each primary&#x27;s epsilon curve only for available biased arms; otherwise explicitly unavailable.
- **Readiness:** Configured contrasts are conditional on supplied readiness and recorded provenance; missing/failed arm or endpoint readiness is not a measured zero. Epsilon contrasts require epsilon\_supported.

Every selected endpoint that is not named in a hypothesis is exploratory, and so are the supervised summaries (intent\_cosine, stouffer\_z\_windows, cumulative\_deviation, blinded\_target\_rank, questionnaire\_descriptives\_by\_belief). Where the harness computes an exploratory endpoint, its result is reported with an effect size and an interval; it never resolves to a verdict. Exploratory results do not by themselves establish a causal consciousness effect.

**Frozen executable contract:** reload this exact JSON into `StatisticalPlan`, verify its hash, and execute unchanged; do not rebuild it from the current registry. The card snapshots inside it carry the registry's own descriptions, which were written for the built-in plan. Where a description names a hypothesis number or calls an endpoint primary or secondary, that does not apply to this study, and a `permutations` task argument of a card is not used: the plan's own `permutations` value is.

## Stopping and exclusion rules

Fixed items and k per available arm; no significance\-based stopping; only the first full run of a study is confirmatory; pilot runs never are. Exclude fallback/degraded/error/aborted samples from clean primary analysis; report taints, counts and sensitivity analysis separately; never delete artifacts.

Missing paired data are not imputed; report denominators and exclusions per arm/card and restrict paired analyses to complete matching units. A hypothesis with fewer than 90% of its planned data analysed is invalid, not negative. No silent retries that replace observed outcomes. Scheduling timers are advisory; every transition into running requires explicit host start/resume. A stopped run is labelled incomplete, not a completed negative finding. Paid-for artifacts are retained or quarantined, never deleted.

The exclusion of error samples has one exception, stated under "Result checks" below: a sample whose attempt ended in an error, and which was generated again and completed after the host resumed the run, is analysed. A resume generates only samples that have no completed reply, so it replaces no observed outcome.

## Result checks

The harness checks every reply and its token records while the run stores them. On an eval that runs on the harness's own runner it also checks every score and every judgement. On an eval that runs through Inspect, Inspect scores and grades the samples itself, and the harness checks neither. This document describes version 1 of these checks. They are fixed by the harness and are the same for every arm and every study: no setting of this study changes them. No check asks a model whether a reply makes sense.

**A flag excludes nothing.** A flag marks a sample and changes nothing else. A flagged sample stays in every analysis exactly as an unflagged one, and no test or verdict reads a flag. The flags are counted for each arm and eval on the results page. The kinds of flag are:

- **empty reply** (empty\_output): The reply has no visible text: once one reasoning block at its start is set aside, nothing is left but whitespace and invisible characters.
- **ended at the token limit** (truncated): The reply ended because it reached the token limit.
- **ends in a loop** (repetition): The reply ends in a loop: the same text of 1 to 200 characters repeated at least 8 times in a row over at least 240 characters. A last copy that is cut short counts as one of the 8, and whitespace at the end of the reply is ignored.
- **damaged characters** (garbled): The reply has at least 20 characters, and at least 5% of them, and at least 3, are replacement characters or control characters other than tab, newline and carriage return, which is what broken text decoding leaves behind.
- **reasoning in the reply** (reasoning\_in\_output): The reply starts with a &lt;think&gt; tag, or has a &lt;/think&gt; tag with no &lt;think&gt; before it, so reasoning text sits where the answer should be.
- **no token log** (tier0\_missing): In a run whose token records come from the engine&#x27;s token log, the request asked the engine for a token log and none arrived; or, in any run, a token came back without a log\-probability. No token records were written for the sample. Its reply, score and judgement stand.
- **draw outside its bracket** (u\_outside\_bracket): For at least one token the random draw lies outside the probability bracket of the token that was sampled. A healthy engine cannot produce this.
- **scorer failed** (score\_error): The card&#x27;s scorer raised an error or returned a value that cannot be stored, so the sample has no score.
- **answer not extracted** (unparsed): The card&#x27;s scorer reports that it could not extract an answer from the reply.
- **no judge reply** (judge\_failed): The judge gave no reply for the sample: the request failed, or the harness could not build the judge prompt or read the reply&#x27;s fields. The judgement is asked again when the run is resumed.
- **judge reply without a score** (judge\_unreadable): The judge replied and no score could be read from the reply. The reply is kept without a score and the judge is not asked again.
- **judge score not allowed** (judge\_out\_of\_range): The score read from the judge&#x27;s reply is not one of the values the rubric allows. The reply is kept without a score and the judge is not asked again.
- **judge reply cut short** (judge\_cut): The judge&#x27;s reply did not end normally, so it may be incomplete.

The checks do not detect the following: a loop with a counter in it; a loop that the model leaves again before the reply ends; reasoning written in any form other than &lt;think&gt; tags; nonsense written in valid Unicode.

**A taint excludes.** Under the exclusion rule above, a tainted sample is left out of the clean analysis. A sample is tainted in these cases:

- stream\_error: its generation ended in an error before the reply was complete.
- engine\_fallback: the engine reported that it fell back from the arm&#x27;s entropy source while the sample was generated.
- qrng\_degraded: it is a sample of a quantum arm, and while it was generated the engine&#x27;s entropy check reported the quantum source as degraded or could not be reached.
- stateless\_row: its token records could not be built from what the engine returned.

One taint is lifted by a completed reply. A stream\_error taint does not exclude a sample that has a completed reply. That is the case when the run was resumed and the sample was generated again: the taint belongs to the attempt that failed, and the reply that completed is analysed. A sample that also carries another taint stays out, and a sample with no completed reply is not analysed.

**What stops a run.** A check stops the run when one of the following holds. Each rule is followed by what Resume, the host's action that continues the run, does after it.

- **generations are failing** (generation\_errors): 8 generations in a row on one arm ended in an error before a reply was complete, or at least half of the last 40 generations of the run did \(looked at once 20 have ended\). On a card that runs through Inspect, one generation that does not complete stops the run, because Inspect cannot go on past a sample without a reply. Nothing that was generated is lost. Resume tries every sample that has no completed reply again, with the keys the run holds at that time. This check then counts again from zero.
- **the quantum source is degraded** (entropy\_degraded): On a quantum arm, 10 samples in a row were tainted for an engine fallback or a degraded quantum source, or 3 samples in a row started while the engine&#x27;s entropy check already reported the source degraded or could not be reached. The tainted samples are complete. They stay in the run, they are excluded from the analysis under the registered rule, and Resume does not generate them again. Resume goes on with the samples that are left. This check then counts again from zero.
- **token records are missing** (tier0\_failed): 10 samples in a row on one arm have no usable token records: each was tainted for its token records or flagged for a missing token log. Those samples are complete and Resume does not generate them again. A sample tainted for its token records is excluded from the analysis under the registered rule. A sample flagged for a missing token log keeps its reply, score and judgement and has no token records. Resume goes on with the samples that are left. This check then counts again from zero.
- **the scorer is failing** (scorer\_errors): The scorer of one card failed on 10 samples in a row. The samples whose scorer failed are complete and have no score. The harness does not score a stored reply again, so Resume cannot recover them. Resume goes on with the samples that are left. This check then counts again from zero.
- **replies are empty** (empty\_outputs): 20 replies in a row on one card, in the order they were stored, were empty, they came from at least 3 prompts, and at least 2 arms each gave at least 5 of them. A reply that has reasoning text and ended at the token limit is not counted. An empty reply is a complete sample: it stays in the run and in the analysis and Resume does not generate it again. Resume goes on with the samples that are left. This check is not applied to the card again in this run.
- **no answer can be extracted** (nothing\_parsed): On a card without an LLM judge, none of the card&#x27;s scored samples so far gave an answer the card&#x27;s scorer could extract, and there are at least 30 of them from at least 2 prompts; or the card&#x27;s queue ended with 10 to 29 scored samples and none of them did. The first sample that gives an answer ends this check for the card. Those samples are complete: they stay in the run as they are, and Resume neither generates nor scores them again. Resume goes on with the samples that are left. This check is not applied to the card again in this run.
- **samples are missing** (unfinished): Generation reached the end of its queue and some arm and card pair has no completed sample, or more than 2% of its planned samples, and at least 3, have no completed reply. The same is checked at the end of judging for judgements without a reply from the judge. Resume tries every sample that has no completed reply, and every judgement that has no reply, again. This check stops a run once for generation and once for judging: if samples are still missing when that part ends again, the run goes on without them.
- **the judge refuses requests** (judge\_rejected): The judge answered a request with HTTP status 401, 403 or 404. When the run holds a judge key and one of its evals is scored by the study&#x27;s judge, one small request with the study&#x27;s judge settings is also made before the first generation, and there a status of 400 counts as well. Nothing that was generated or judged is lost. Supply a judge key that works and Resume: every judgement that has no reply is asked again. The judge model and its settings are frozen in the study, so Resume cannot fix a model or a setting the provider refuses. This check is made again after Resume.
- **the judge is not answering** (judge\_unusable): 10 judge calls in a row got no reply, or at least half of the last 40 judge calls did \(looked at once 20 have ended\). Judgements that got a reply are kept. Resume asks every judgement that has no reply again. This check then counts again from zero.
- **no judge reply can be read** (nothing\_judged): No score could be read from any of the first 30 judge replies for one card. A reply that was received is final: those replies are kept without a score and the judge is not asked again for them. Resume goes on with the judgements that are left. This check is not applied to the card again in this run.
- **the judge phase failed** (judge\_phase\_error): The judge phase ended on an error the harness did not expect. Every row already written is kept. Resume starts the judge phase again and asks every judgement that has no reply. If the same error comes back the run stops again: this check is never switched off.

A stop is a pause, not an abort. No new sample or judgement is started, those under way finish, and nothing that was stored is removed. The run does not continue by itself: the host resumes it or aborts it. No completed reply is generated again and no judge reply that was received is asked for again because of what it says, with one exception: where an eval reads the judge's reply with its own code and that code fails on a reply, the judgement counts as failed and is asked again on resume. Every stop is stored with the run, with its rule, its counts and the time at which the run was resumed, and the stops of a run are listed on the results page.

Pre-session sheep–goat belief rating on a 1–7 scale and state check on a 1–5 scale; required post-session adapted coincidence survey. Exact wording/scales are governed by the frozen questionnaire asset, not invented here. If its hash is missing, the questionnaire is not frozen. Descriptives are grouped by belief item; multiple observers in the same session do not increase the independent sample count. Intention is shown only to observers, not inserted into target-model prompts.

## Data sharing

Public by default: frozen config, preregistration, script-generated statistics/figures and consented pseudonymous session data. Raw data licence **CC-BY-4.0**; prose **CC-BY-SA-4.0**; code **Apache-2.0**. Observers consent before participation to publishing intention text, timing and questionnaire responses; avoid personal identifiers. Provider/judge credentials are never included. Withdrawal labels retained artifacts rather than erasing paid-for evidence.

## Validity limits

The consciousness/intention mechanism is a hypothesis, not an established physical fact. QRNG-vs-PRNG differences alone would not demonstrate that mechanism. Forward-pass nondeterminism, unequal compute/scheduling, observer selection and timing, prompt dependence, judge/embedding bias, evaluation awareness and told-source priming are nuisance factors. Equivalent sampling is a conditional engineering claim, not proof of quantum purity or of consciousness influence. Raw-logprob fallback does not recover post-truncation probabilities or PIT residuals. T0-a and T4-l require engine logs; T0-c is only partially available on API logprobs. A public render request does not verify the submitted readiness evidence. The sample-size ratings are bounds computed before the run, not achieved power. Arms are not randomised against each other in time, so a drift of the engine or of the entropy source during the run is not separated from the difference between the sources.
